source_text.Q-1042: MEDIUM, owner CI lane (follow-up of Q-1037, the next lever after sharding). Reported by the supervisor 2026-10-08. Evidence: ExUnit reports ~0.5 s average per test and ~66 min of cumulative test work per backend run (7.7k tests); a large share is believed to be the per-test tenant schema clone from tenant_template (CREATE SCHEMA ... LIKE tenant_template... for every table, see the LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE setup/teardown log lines and the 'tenant_template_build' schemas): cost per test = DDL for every table of the template plus DROP SCHEMA CASCADE at teardown. NOT yet measured: step 1 is to instrument (time per clone, number of tables cloned, share of test time) on one partition, step 2 choose the lever: (a) clone only the tables the test needs, (b) share a read-only tenant across tests that do not mutate it (async-safe), (c) a pooled tenant per module with truncate-reset, (d) Postgres schema cloning via CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE or a faster mechanism; keep isolation guarantees (no cross-test leakage, the ISS-0410-class isolation bugs). Each step measured before/after; mutation proof that isolation still holds (a test that leaves data behind must not leak into the next). Overlap check 2026-10-08: Q-1037 is the umbrella; ISS-0410 (isolation failure, blocked) is background, not a duplicate.

task.description:
WF-03 Step 2b: independent hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's design for ISS-1042 / Q-1042 (equivalent of WF-02 Step 1b). Follow your role file .claude/agents/code-design-validator.md.

DESIGN UNDER REVIEW: lib/letflow/design/iss1042-pooled-tenant-fixture.md. Diagnosis it designs against: docs/issues/ISS-1042.yaml. Source of acceptance criteria: this handoff's task.acceptance_criteria (4 items).

VERIFY (independently, from the files, not from the designer's summary):
1. Every acceptance criterion is covered by a concrete design element (measurement plan with 5+5 runs; isolation mutation proof; one lever; no CI check-name change, no paid runners).
2. The design contains no implementation code beyond signatures/@specs/SQL sketches the role file permits.
3. It is unambiguous enough that a weaker model could build it: every function has name, @spec, behaviour, failure mode; the reset algorithm is stepwise and ordering-safe against FKs; no 'TBD' that blocks building. Open questions (section 14) must each have a stated default and a stated consequence, and the design must be correct under either answer to OQ-1/OQ-2 (whether test-process writes commit under DataCase checkout + Sandbox.mode(:auto)). Check that claim by reading test/support/ (DataCase, TenantFixture) yourself.
4. The design's description of the CURRENT code (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, test/support/tenant_template.ex, the single dispatch point, the 22 template: :replay sites, DDL/drop tests) is factually accurate: spot-check at least 8 specific claims against the files and quote what you found.
5. Leak classes: try to find a cross-test leakage path the design's M1-M12 mutations do NOT cover (public-schema rows keyed by tenant, sequences, triggers, advisory locks, ETS/Registry/process state, caches keyed by tenant id, files). Each real gap is a finding.
6. Fail-safe: confirm the design can never return a dirty tenant (falls back to fresh clone or raises). Look for a TOCTOU between the cleanliness proof and the hand-out.
7. owned_modules in section 12 are complete and minimal; named existing tests-to-stay-green exist.
You may run read-only commands and mix compile. Do not edit the design (never edit what you validate); report findings with severity BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR in result.issues. FAIL on any BLOCKER or an unfixable-by-implementer MAJOR; PASS_WITH_FINDINGS style minor items go in issues with result.status PASS.
Complete the handoff per docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md. Commit your handoff completion and push to feature/WF03-ISS1042-20261012. Do not edit handoffs/registry.json or handoffs/orchestrator.log.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented measurement: clone time per test, tables per clone, share of total test time (numbers quoted)
One lever implemented with before/after wall time of the test phase (5 runs each, run ids)
Isolation proof: a test leaving data behind does not leak into the next test (mutation test)
No change to required check names; no paid runners

result.summary: FAIL: 2 BLOCKER and 4 MAJOR findings against lib/letflow/design/iss1042-pooled-tenant-fixture.md, 5 MINOR. Covered and verified: all four acceptance criteria map to concrete design elements (criterion 1 numbers re-derived against docs/issues/ISS-1042.yaml: 839/711/3107 ms, 74.0%/80.4%, 114/51/39, 204 of 403; 5+5 interleaved runs with run ids; one lever; no .github change, no check-name change, no paid runners), no function bodies (signatures, @specs, SQL sketches only), every OQ has a default. 13 claims about current code spot-checked and accurate (e.g. tenant_fixture.ex:237 Sandbox.mode(:auto) first line; :247-263 tenant insert and on_exit before provisioning; :492-504 three teardown statements; tenant_template.ex:788-805 seed copies and :807-818 Registration insert as last step; :704-722 do_clone_with_retry; assert_clone_parity!/3 at :253; data_case.ex reads tags[:async] and sets {:shared, self()}; the three adopters are DataCase async: false; no BEFORE TRUNCATE trigger in migrations; start_scheduler/start_service_task_dispatcher false in config/test.exs; named tests-to-stay-green files exist; 5 ETS/persistent_term holders confirmed by grep). The design fails on isolation soundness, which is the point of the issue: the runtime cleanliness proof is blind to name/count-preserving DDL (F1) and to writers outliving the test (F2); the seed restore (F3), rebuild refresh (F4), first-acquire rule (F5) and teardown mode (F6) are contradictory or unspecified. F1 and F2 need a design decision (what the fingerprint is, what the residual-risk/mitigation is), not an implementer judgement call. The design file was not edited.

issues.description: F1 structure fingerprint (design 4.2.1 / 4.3.1) is names plus COUNTS of indexes/constraints only, so DDL that preserves names and counts is invisible and never reset: ALTER TABLE .. DISABLE TRIGGER on audit_entries/repository_artifacts/artifact_versions (immutability triggers stay disabled for every later test in the module), ADD/DROP/ALTER COLUMN (type, default, NOT NULL), drop-and-recreate of an index or CHECK/FK constraint under the same name or with count unchanged, ALTER SEQUENCE INCREMENT/START, table/column comments. TRUNCATE does not undo any of it and the verify pass (4.3.5) compares the same weak fingerprint, so INV-P1 and 9.4 'never returns a dirty tenant' are false for this class. M8 covers only CREATE TABLE and DROP TRIGGER. Design must define the fingerprint as a digest of definitions (pg_get_triggerdef incl. tgenabled, pg_get_constraintdef, pg_get_indexdef, per-column type/default/nullability from pg_attribute/pg_attrdef, trigger function defs, sequence parameters) or run the same dimensions as assert_clone_parity! in the runtime verify, and add mutation classes for DISABLE TRIGGER and column/index/constraint alteration with unchanged counts.

F2 late-writer / TOCTOU not closed, and a new leak class is unaudited. (a) 4.3.5 verifies in a separate transaction after COMMIT and the result is handed out with no lock or re-check, so any process still alive from the previous test can write between verify and the test's first use; INV-P1/9.4 ('no code path returns a slot whose cleanliness was not proven in that acquire') is true only at the verify instant and the doc presents it as unconditional. M10 simulates only a write between recycle_pool! and the next acquire, not one after verify. (b) A fresh tenant id per test made straggler processes harmless (they hit a dropped schema or a different id); a pooled id makes them corrupt the NEXT test. Section 6 audits only ETS/persistent_term holders. lib has fire-and-forget workers not considered: Task.Supervisor.start_child in lib/letflow/obs/alerts.ex:484 (Letflow.Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor) and lib/letflow/login_discovery/dispatch.ex:56 (LoginDiscovery.TaskSupervisor, async_nolink at :126), plus any un-awaited Task.async/Task.start in adopter modules (store_test.exs has Task.async at 338-339, 1151, 1162). Under Sandbox :auto their writes commit. Design must (i) restate INV-P1 precisely, (ii) add an adopter audit rule and result for spawned/supervised processes that can touch the tenant schema, (iii) specify a mitigation or a detection (e.g. second probe immediately before return plus an end-of-test dirty-after check that fails the owning test loudly), and add a mutation for a post-verify write.

F3 seed restore is specified two contradictory ways: 4.3.4.3 says INSERT INTO <clone>.<seed> SELECT * FROM tenant_template.<seed> (the do_clone steps 7-8 statements), while 4.4 says restore re-inserts from the baseline's captured rows as an Elixir term ('Resolved here'), and OQ-6 says fall back to the live template if the term is large. Re-inserting from a term requires re-encoding uuid/jsonb/timestamp columns of event_type_registry, and clone_baseline is declared @opaque with clone_state.seed_digests holding only {count, md5}, so the rows are not even in the stated shape. Pick one mechanism and state its ISS-0842 ordering assumption.

F4 rebuild path leaves state refresh unspecified. rebuild_clone_schema! (2.2) drops the schema, deletes the Registration row and re-clones; do_clone inserts a NEW Registration via Registration.changeset (new id, new provisioned_at/migrations_applied_at, tenant_template.ex:807-818), so registration_snapshot (3.2) is stale and the immediate verify (tenant_schemas row == snapshot, 4.3.5) would fail, causing a raise. The design never says that after a rebuild the worker re-runs assert_schema_complete!, recaptures baseline, re-snapshots the registration row, bumps generation, and which process runs it. M8/M9 expect 'generation incremented and clean' and cannot pass as written.

F5 internal contradiction on the first acquire: section 4 preamble says the first acquire of a :clean slot 'skips straight to hand-out' (no probe, no verify), while INV-P1 (13) and 9.4 say a pooled provisioned_tenant! returns only after a verify pass in that acquire. The probe costs 3.6 ms; state one rule (recommend verify always).

F6 pool teardown (3.4) and the module-end on_exit never set Sandbox.mode(Repo, :auto). DataCase sets {:shared, self()} per non-async test; if the module's last test did not call provisioned_tenant! (which is what flips to :auto) the on_exit/worker statements run with mode {:shared, dead_pid} or :manual and raise DBConnection.OwnershipError, leaving the schema to the reaper and failing the module. Specify that teardown first calls Sandbox.mode(:auto) (noting its global whole-pool check-in side effect, ISS-0113 9.1).

M-a OQ-1 is resolvable now and the 'correct under both answers' claim is not true for section 9 under answer A. From deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex only explicit Sandbox.checkout/2 runs post_checkout begin (lines 544-551, 658); Manager auto-checkouts under :auto are not wrapped, and DataCase's {:shared, self()} -> fixture :auto is a mode change that checks in the DataCase connection (ISS-0113 9.2-9.3). Test-process writes therefore commit (answer B), consistent with the measured 41 ms DROP SCHEMA teardown (a no-op DROP would be ~1 ms). Under A, 9.2's 'mutate, recycle, assert pristine' would fail (uncommitted rows seen only by the test process, row locks block the worker TRUNCATE until lock_timeout). Record answer B in the design and drop the 'both' claim. identity_id_hardening_test.exs:454 comment 'DDL rolls back' is stale.

M-b factual: design 1.2 says 52 test files use PlatformTenantFixture.three_tenants!; actual: 52 files reference PlatformTenantFixture, 27 reference three_tenants! (grep). Design 7 says '22+ template: :replay sites (29 files with the literal)'; actual: 29 occurrences in 14 files (two of those files are test/specs/*.md, one is test/support/tenant_fixture.ex).

M-c factual: expected_tenant_tables/0 has 49 entries (tenant_fixture.ex:127-177), plus the separately created schema_migrations = 50 CREATE TABLE (LIKE) statements; the design's '50 x CREATE TABLE (LIKE ...)' is correct as statements, but the diagnosis label '50 expected_tenant_tables' is not. Section 5.1's informative public-table list omits public.secrets (tenant_id uuid, no FK, caught only by rule (b)) and event_history_retirement_outcomes (FK to tenants, on_delete :nothing).

M-d handoff dispatch drift for ORCH: context.owned_modules omits store_test.exs, the new test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs, docs/issues/ISS-1042.yaml and docs/anti-patterns.md that design 12.1 requires, and lists tenant_fixture_test.exs which the design makes conditional. started_at was null at claim; left null per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL 1.2.

M-e minor under-specification: attach_pool! must run before any setup that calls provisioned_tenant! (identity_id_hardening_test.exs:49 calls three_tenants! from setup; wrong order silently takes the default path or, because attach resets the claim counter, hands {shape,0} out twice); M2 names 'definition_sequence/events global seq' as an example instead of one concrete table and sequence; where pool_dirty_report/1 executes (test process vs worker) is unstated.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER, iteration 1 of 3: resolve F1-F6 in lib/letflow/design/iss1042-pooled-tenant-fixture.md (F1 definitional fingerprint plus new mutations; F2 restate INV-P1, add process audit rule and post-verify detection; F3 one seed-restore mechanism; F4 rebuild refresh steps; F5 verify-always; F6 teardown sets :auto), record OQ-1 = committed per Sandbox source, fix the MINOR facts, then re-dispatch CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR step 02b.
